experiments.title: Intra-industry lead-lag — big firms lead small firms in the same industry
experiments.hypothesis: Within an industry, returns of the largest firms predict following weeks' returns of the smallest firms in the same industry (reverse does not hold), driven by slow diffusion of industry information and sluggish adjustment to negative news.

literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Within an industry, returns of the largest firms predict following weeks' returns of the smallest firms in the same industry (reverse does not hold), driven by slow diffusion of industry information and sluggish adjustment to negative news.

experiments.title: Tail-risk beta — loadings on the common tail-risk factor (Kelly-Jiang)
experiments.hypothesis: A monthly tail-risk measure estimated from the cross-section of firm-level crashes (pooled tail exponent) is time-varying; stocks with high loadings on past tail risk earn an annual three-factor alpha 5.4% higher than stocks with low loadings.

literature_intake.source: Kelly & Jiang, Review of Financial Studies 27 (2014) 2841-2871
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: A monthly tail-risk measure estimated from the cross-section of firm-level crashes (pooled tail exponent) is time-varying; stocks with high loadings on past tail risk earn an annual three-factor alpha 5.4% higher than stocks with low loadings.

experiments.title: Insider net buying — open-market purchases by officers and directors
experiments.hypothesis: Firms with extensive insider open-market purchases outperform firms with extensive insider sales over the following 12 months (7.8% raw, 4.8% after size and book-to-market controls); predictive content is in purchases, not sales.

literature_intake.source: Lakonishok & Lee, Review of Financial Studies 14 (2001) 79-111
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Firms with extensive insider open-market purchases outperform firms with extensive insider sales over the following 12 months (7.8% raw, 4.8% after size and book-to-market controls); predictive content is in purchases, not sales.

experiments.acceptance_criteria: TBD — frozen gate to be written before any run
limitations: Signal must be keyed to the Form 4 FILING date, never the transaction date; transaction-date measurement credits outsiders with information not yet public.

Paper: effect is more informative in smaller firms and purchases tilt to small/high book-to-market names — a 250-name large-cap-tilted universe may dilute it; preregistration should state the expected cross-sectional spread in insider activity on this universe first.

Long-only form (overweight intensive net buyers) is the honest version; the paper gives the sales/short side little support and a fabricated short leg would collide with the killed short-side daily family.
Requires a new public SEC EDGAR Form 4 route (free, no vendor).
Dedupe PASS: no registry experiment uses regulatory filings as a signal.

experiments.title: Expected idiosyncratic skewness (Boyer-Mitton-Vorkink)
experiments.hypothesis: Expected idiosyncratic skewness and returns are negatively correlated: the Fama-French alpha of a low-expected-skewness quintile exceeds that of a high-expected-skewness quintile by 1.00% per month, where expected skewness is forecast by a cross-sectional model rather than taken as raw lagged skewness.

literature_intake.source: Boyer, Mitton & Vorkink, Review of Financial Studies 23 (2010) 169-202
literature_intake.finding: Harvest intake only; claim as published, not tested by us.
literature_intake.hypothesis_derived: Expected idiosyncratic skewness and returns are negatively correlated: the Fama-French alpha of a low-expected-skewness quintile exceeds that of a high-expected-skewness quintile by 1.00% per month, where expected skewness is forecast by a cross-sectional model rather than taken as raw lagged skewness.
